:::{#exm-uncorrelated-not-indpt}
#### Zero covariance without independence

The converse of @thm-indpt-uncorrelated is false.
Let $X$ take the values $-1$, $0$, and $1$ with probability $1/3$ each,
and let $Y = X^2$.
Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{X} &= (-1 + 0 + 1)/3 \\
&= 0,
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
XY &= X^3 \\
&= X,
\end{aligned}
$$

so:

$$
\ba
\Cov{X,Y}
&= \E{XY} - \E{X}\E{Y}
&& \text{(alternative formula for covariance)} \\
&= \E{X} - \E{X}\E{Y}
&& \text{(} XY = X^3 \text{ and } X^3 = X \text{ on } \set{-1, 0, 1} \text{)} \\
&= 0 - 0 \cd \E{Y}
&& \text{(} \E{X} = 0 \text{)} \\
&= 0
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

But $X$ and $Y$ are not independent: $Y$ is a function of $X$, and

$$
\begin{aligned}
\P(X = 0, Y = 0) &= \P(X = 0) \\
&= \tfrac{1}{3},
\end{aligned}
$$

while

$$
\begin{aligned}
\P(X = 0)\,\P(Y = 0) &= \tfrac{1}{3} \cd \tfrac{1}{3} \\
&= \tfrac{1}{9}.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
